column1: # Section-level exclusions for the normative-requirement coverage audit.
# specs/audit-scope.tsv decides whether a specification imposes obligations at
# all. This file is finer grained: it drops individual sections of an in-scope
# specification whose requirements are addressed to an actor Vouch is not, or
# cover a feature Vouch does not implement by design.
# An excluded statement is not "untested" -- it is not owed. It never enters the
# in-scope denominator and never lands in specs/coverage-baseline.tsv, so the
# backlog stays a list of real work.
# section_prefix matches a section and everything beneath it: "4" excludes 4,
# 4.8 and 4.8.1, but not 40. The reason column is required and must say what
# makes the section inapplicable, with the evidence -- the next person to read
# it needs to be able to check the claim, not just take it.
# crates/vouch-tests/tests/spec_coverage.rs enforces two rules that keep this
# file honest:
#   1. An exclusion matching no statement fails the build. Sections get
#      renumbered when a spec is re-cached, and a stale exclusion would
#      silently stop covering anything.
#   2. An excluded section that a test cites fails the build. The exclusion
#      claims Vouch has no obligation there while a test asserts behavior, so
#      one of the two is wrong and a human has to say which.

rfc6265
column3: Section 5 is "User Agent Requirements" -- the browser-side cookie storage and parsing algorithm. Vouch is a server (Section 4); the CLI writes a Netscape cookie file for curl interop and implements no part of the UA algorithm.

column1: rfc7515
column3: JWS JSON Serialization. Vouch uses compact serialization throughout; no code path produces or parses the general or flattened JSON forms.

column1: rfc7515
column3: TLS requirements for retrieving key material named by the "jku" and "x5u" header parameters. The section is scoped by its opening sentence, "Implementations supporting the \"jku\" and/or \"x5u\" Header Parameters MUST support TLS"; Vouch supports neither, dereferences no header-supplied URL (grep for jku/x5u across crates/*/src returns nothing), and pins that refusal in test_rfc7515_header_supplied_key_material_is_not_a_key_source.

column1: rfc7518
column3: JWE key management algorithms (RSAES, ECDH-ES, AES-KW, PBES2). Vouch implements no JWE: services/oidc/jar.rs rejects five-part tokens, and the only algorithms produced or verified anywhere are ES256, RS256, PS256, EdDSA and HS256.

column1: rfc7518
column3: JWE content encryption algorithms (AES-CBC-HMAC, AES-GCM). Same reason as section 4 -- no JWE support.

column1: rfc9700
column3: Refresh token guidance. Vouch issues no refresh tokens by design; see the section 4.14 row.

column1: rfc9700
column3: Refresh token replay detection, rotation and binding. Vouch issues no refresh tokens by design -- services/oidc/grant_type.rs has no refresh grant, and services/oidc/registration.rs treats refresh_token as registration-only ("accepted in registration, though never issued"). The underlying threat is answered by short-lived DPoP-bound access tokens with no long-lived credential to replay.

column1: rfc9700
column3: Attacks on in-browser communication flows -- authorization responses delivered by postMessage instead of HTTP redirects. Not implemented: no occurrence of postMessage or web_message in the workspace, ResponseMode has no such variant, and response_modes_supported advertises only query, form_post and the JARM forms. Pinned by test_rfc9700_authorization_response_is_never_delivered_in_browser, which cites the conditional requirement in section 2.6 rather than this section.

column1: webauthn-2
column3: CredentialRequestOptions dictionary extension -- addressed to the client, not the Relying Party.

column1: webauthn-2
column3: The authenticatorMakeCredential operation -- addressed to the authenticator, not the Relying Party.
